newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end flat, Ericsson and forestry gain.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end flat, Ericsson and forestry gain.

text.p: Swedish shares ended little changed on Wednesday with strong gains for telecoms group Ericsson and forestry shares being counterbalanced by falls in drugs major Astra.
The Stockholm bourse's general index edged 0.04 percent higher to 2,889.86 in turnover of 6.04 billion crowns.
Ericsson was by far the most traded share with turnover reaching almost 1.3 billion crowns.
The share jumped 5.5 crowns to 291.5, boosted by market reports that investment bank Merrill Lynch had raised its profit forecasts for the group.

Sources told Reuters Merrill Lynch had a target price of 350 crowns for Ericsson and that it had raised its 1997 profit forecast to 9.70 crowns a share from nine crowns and its 1998 estimates to 13.50 crowns a share from 11.50.
The forestry sector rallied, up 1.95 percent on market talk of U.S. pulp price hikes.
"As far as I know three companies have announced price hikes from $580 a tonne to $630 -- Weyerhaeuser, Stone Container and Georgia Pacific," Anders Jansson at Rottneros told Reuters.
Stora rose 3.5 to 118.5 and AssiDoman edged 1.5 higher to 219 while SCA slipped one crown to 159.
Drugs shares performed poorly with Astra dropping four crowns to 126.5 and Pharmacia & Upjohn sliding 5.5 crowns to 272.
